summary: President said the ‘violent Fighter and Warrior’ plus some UFC brawlers would ‘defend us from the Lunatic Left’ Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the presid
summary_zh: 总统表示，“暴力战士和战士”加上一些 UFC 斗殴者将“保卫我们免受疯狂左派的侵害”唐纳德·特朗普已提供了 Wh 的职位
body_en: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary | Trump administration
President said the ‘violent Fighter and Warrior’ plus some UFC brawlers would ‘defend us from the Lunatic Left’
Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday.

Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries.
From the Octagon to Quantico: UFC teaching the FBI to fight is its latest tie to Trump world

Trump added that he asked White, a vocal supporter who campaigned for him in 2024, to bring six UFC fighters with him to serve as press aides. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!”

It was unclear if the job offer was part of an actual plan, or an attention-grabbing stunt from a president desperate to change the subject from the huge losses suffered by his party in elections this week.

There was no immediate response from White, who, some observers noted, might hesitate to leave a lucrative role running the UFC, which has earned him a fortune estimated to be in excess of $600m , for a job in government service that pays $195,000 a year.

The president’s post was illustrated by seven images, including what appeared to be an AI-generated image of White behind the presidential seal in a press room, and photographs of the six UFC fighters whom Trump fantasizes about deploying to deal with reporters who ask him awkward questions: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov (who are both from a Muslim-majority region of Russia), Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison – whose last name was mistakenly rendered as “Harris” by the president.

In his post, Trump acknowledged that two of his dream hires, Makhachev and Nurmagomedov, are not Americans, but he did not mention that Nurmagomedov is reportedly close to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, or that Makhachev has spoken out in defense of Palestinian civilians killed by Israel in Gaza. In 2023, Makhachev also celebrated a victory in one fight by saying , “Alhamdulillah,” the Arabic phrase for “praise be to God” used by Muslims. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was criticized in the rightwing media for using that same Arabic phrase in his victory speech this week.

The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention .

The role of White House press secretary has been vacant for three weeks, since Trump’s previous pick, far-right commentator Katie Zacharia , was forced to resign after trying, and failing, to dodge questions about why she described herself as an attorney despite having failed the bar exam.
body_zh: 特朗普表示，他邀请 UFC 老板达纳·怀特 (Dana White) 担任他的新任白宫新闻秘书特朗普政府
总统表示，“暴力战士和战士”加上一些 UFC 斗殴者将“保卫我们免受疯狂左派的侵害”
总统在周六的社交媒体帖子中表示，唐纳德·特朗普已向终极格斗锦标赛首席执行官达纳·怀特提供白宫新闻秘书的职位。
怀特今年 6 月在白宫上演了一场笼斗奇观，以纪念总统 80 岁生日，特朗普将怀特描述为“一名暴力斗士和战士”，这与任何用来描述以前新闻秘书的资历都不同。
从八角笼到匡蒂科：UFC 教 FBI 格斗是其与特朗普世界的最新联系
特朗普补充说，他要求曾在 2024 年为他竞选的怀特带六名 UFC 选手一起担任新闻助理。怀特是他的直言不讳的支持者。特朗普写道：“我们需要这些人来保护我们免受疯狂左派的侵害。” “达娜，请接受这份工作！”
目前还不清楚这份工作机会是否是实际计划的一部分，或者是一位总统为了转移话题而采取的引人注目的噱头，因为他的政党在本周的选举中遭受了巨大损失。
怀特没有立即做出回应，一些观察人士指出，怀特可能会犹豫是否要放弃管理 UFC 的有利可图的职位，而 UFC 为他带来了估计超过 6 亿美元的财富，而去从事年薪 195,000 美元的政府服务工作。

总统的帖子由七张图片进行说明，其中包括由人工智能生成的新闻发布室中总统印章背后的怀特图像，以及特朗普幻想部署的六名 UFC 战士的照片，特朗普幻想部署这些战士来应对向他提出尴尬问题的记者：伊斯兰·马哈乔夫 (Islam Makhachev) 和哈比卜·努尔马戈梅多夫 (Khabib Nurmagomedov)（两人都来自俄罗斯穆斯林占多数的地区）、贾斯汀·盖特杰 (Justin Gaethje)、丹尼尔·科米尔 (Daniel Cormier)、阿曼达·努内斯 (Amanda Nunes) 和凯拉·哈里森 (Kayla Harrison)（姓氏为被总统误译为“哈里斯”。

特朗普在帖子中承认，他梦寐以求的两名雇员马哈乔夫和努尔马戈梅多夫都不是美国人，但他没有提到据报道努尔马戈梅多夫与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京关系密切，也没有提到马哈乔夫曾公开捍卫在加沙被以色列杀害的巴勒斯坦平民。 2023 年，马哈乔夫还通过说“Alhamdulillah”来庆祝一场战斗的胜利，这是穆斯林使用的阿拉伯语，意思是“赞美真主”。民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德因在本周的胜利演讲中使用同样的阿拉伯短语而受到右翼媒体的批评。
在最近的中期选举前夕，白宫播放了一系列由纳税人资助的支持特朗普的广告中的第一个，广告的结尾是特朗普生日那天 UFC 比赛的画面，以及怀特对他的评价，可以听到怀特说：“他是我一生中见过的最坚强、最有韧性的人。”怀特在 2024 年总统竞选期间多次使用这个表述来形容特朗普，最引人注目的是在共和党全国代表大会上赞扬特朗普。
自从特朗普之前挑选的极右翼评论员凯蒂·扎卡里亚(Katie Zacharia)试图回避有关她为何在律师资格考试未及格的情况下称自己为律师的问题后，被迫辞职，但未能成功，白宫新闻秘书一职已空缺三周。

title_en: Stephen Miller, architect of Trump’s immigration crackdown, to become White House chief of staff
title_zh: 特朗普移民镇压策划者斯蒂芬·米勒将出任白宫办公厅主任
summary: US president confirms Susie Wiles, current chief of staff and first woman to serve in the role, will step down Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, will become his new White House chie
summary_zh: 美国总统确认现任幕僚长、第一位担任该职位的女性苏西·怀尔斯 (Susie Wiles) 将辞去美国政坛直播——最新动态
body_en: US president confirms Susie Wiles, current chief of staff and first woman to serve in the role, will step down

Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, will become his new White House chief of staff days after Republicans lost control of the US Congress in US midterm elections.
The president announced the extraordinary appointment on Friday, confirming that Susie Wiles – his current chief of staff, and the first woman to serve in the role – had been ousted.
In a social media ‌post, Trump called Miller, 41, “one of ​my most trusted advisors” and praised Wiles for doing “an ⁠outstanding job”. Miller will begin on Monday.
Wiles, 69, reportedly handed in her resignation on Thursday night and said in a social media post that serving Trump “has been the honor of a lifetime”.

Holding an umbrella, Trump emerged from the White House South Portico on Friday for a trip to Florida. “I wanted to make a change,” he said. “I think Susie’s done a very good job ... Stephen’s been great, and we’ve got to make moves.”
“Stephen’s been with me from the beginning. He gets it,” the president said. “Very good politically and he’s a very good man. He’ll do a great job. Great manager.”
Republicans hoping to succeed Trump in 2028 dissect midterm rout
Trump then boarded the Marine One helicopter, followed by Miller, secretary of state Marco Rubio and close aide Natalie Harp.
In a statement, Wiles added: “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”
She said her commitment to “the President and the mission” will not change.

Miller posted on X that he was “honored beyond words” to serve as Trump’s chief of staff. He added: “The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic.”
But a growing chorus of Democrats condemned the appointment.

Hakeem Jeffries, who is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House, posted: “Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands. His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor. Fire him today.”

Chuck Schumer, likely to be the next majority leader of the Senate, wrote: “Donald Trump learned nothing from his historic defeat. Stephen Miller is the architect of the most barbaric, inhumane policies of this administration. Trump couldn’t have made a worse choice. Our Democratic majorities will fight him every step of the way.”

Miller’s appointment is the first sign of a shake-up at the White House following Republicans’ catastrophic defeat in the midterms. His record as a far-right firebrand implies that Trump is preparing for an aggressive fight against congressional Democrats’ oversight and investigations.

Chris Whipple, author of The Gatekeepers: How the White House Chiefs of Staff Define Every Presidency , told CNN: “It’s almost a declaration of war by Trump … He [Miller] only knows one gear and that’s full-throttle, full steam ahead over the cliff.”
David Axelrod, a veteran Democratic strategist, added on X : “For those who hoped the @POTUS might pivot to work with the incoming Congress, the appointment of Miller is a bucket of ICE cold water.”

Miller is one of the most polarising figures in the administration and one of Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, having joined his 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter. He is a former aide to the former senator Jeff Sessions of Alabama, who would go on to serve as Trump’s first attorney general.
body_zh: 美国总统确认现任幕僚长、第一位担任该职务的女性苏西·怀尔斯 (Susie Wiles) 将辞职
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)最具争议的助手、全面打击移民行动的策划者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)将在共和党在美国中期选举中失去对美国国会的控制权几天后成为他的新任白宫办公厅主任。
总统周五宣布了这一非凡任命，确认现任幕僚长、第一位担任该职位的女性苏西·怀尔斯 (Susie Wiles) 已被罢免。
在社交媒体帖子中，特朗普称 41 岁的米勒是“我最值得信赖的顾问之一”，并称赞怀尔斯做得“非常出色”。米勒将于周一开始。
据报道，69 岁的怀尔斯于周四晚递交了辞呈，并在社交媒体帖子中表示，为特朗普服务“是一生的荣幸”。
周五，特朗普撑着雨伞从白宫南门廊出来前往佛罗里达州。 “我想做出改变，”他说。 “我认为苏西做得很好......斯蒂芬很棒，我们必须采取行动。”
“斯蒂芬从一开始就和我在一起。他明白了，”总统说。 “政治上非常出色，他是一个非常好的人。他会做得很好。伟大的经理。”
希望在 2028 年接替特朗普的共和党人剖析中期选举溃败
随后，特朗普登上了海军陆战队一号直升机，米勒、国务卿马可·卢比奥和亲密助手娜塔莉·哈普紧随其后。
怀尔斯在一份声明中补充道：“我很自豪能够成为我们共同取得的成就的一部分，从保护边境安全、减税到加强我们的经济和实现美国优先。”
她表示，她对“总统和使命”的承诺不会改变。
米勒在 X 上发帖表示，他对担任特朗普的幕僚长感到“难以言表的荣幸”。他补充道：“现在的使命比以往任何时候都更加明确：全心全意地支持我们的总统并保卫这个伟大的共和国。”
但越来越多的民主党人齐声谴责这一任命。
即将成为众议院第一位黑人议长的哈基姆·杰弗里斯发帖称：“斯蒂芬·米勒是一个危险的仇外分子和鲁莽的极端分子，他的手上沾满了美国人的鲜血。他在政府中的存在应该像恶性肿瘤一样被根除。今天就解雇他。”
可能成为下一任参议院多数党领袖的查克·舒默写道：“唐纳德·特朗普从他的历史性失败中没有学到任何教训。斯蒂芬·米勒是本届政府最野蛮、最不人道的政策的缔造者。特朗普不可能做出更糟糕的选择。我们的民主党多数派将一路与他作斗争。”
米勒的任命是共和党在中期选举中惨败后白宫进行改组的第一个迹象。他作为极右煽动者的记录表明，特朗普正在准备积极对抗国会民主党的监督和调查。
《守门人：白宫幕僚长如何定义每一位总统》一书的作者克里斯·惠普尔 (Chris Whipple) 告诉 CNN：“这几乎是特朗普的宣战……他（米勒）只知道一个档位，而这就是全速前进、全速冲向悬崖。”
资深民主党策略师戴维·阿克塞尔罗德 (David Axelrod) 在 X 上补充道：“对于那些希望 @POTUS 转向与即将上任的国会合作的人来说，米勒的任命简直是 ICE 的一桶冷水。”
米勒是政府中最两极分化的人物之一，也是特朗普最亲密、任职时间最长的顾问之一，曾作为演讲撰稿人参加了他的 2016 年总统竞选活动。他是阿拉巴马州前参议员杰夫塞申斯的前助手，塞申斯后来担任特朗普的第一任司法部长。

body_en: Judge to appoint special master to determine whether Trump lawyers purposely misled her over golf course | Washington DC
Ana Reyes wants to know whether federal officials lied about extent of renovation plans at East Potomac golf course

A federal judge said on Saturday that she intended to appoint an ex-top federal prosecutor who served during Donald Trump’s first term to investigate whether she was purposely misled by lawyers and administration officials over changes to a historic public golf course in Washington DC .

Jessie Liu, a former US attorney for the District of Columbia, would examine whether officials with the interior department and the National Park Service and attorneys with the Department of Justice violated ethics or misled US district judge Ana Reyes during the course of the civil case that was initiated with a lawsuit in February by the DC Preservation League and two golfers.

The lawsuit challenges one of the US president’s flurry of construction projects around the nation’s capital – in this case, the renovation of a public golf facility along the Potomac River, which is less high-profile that some of his other plans but had still riled many.

The Republican administration plans to close the East Potomac golf course and park on 15 November with the intention of constructing what it has called a “World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events”.

An injunction issued by Reyes last month temporarily bars the government from removing or damaging any additional trees on the course and ordered the administration to give 10 days’ notice in writing before making any “irreparable modification” to any “forms or features” of the course while the lawsuit is active.

Reyes is now giving each side a chance to be heard on her plan to name Liu as special master in the case. They must do so in writing by Friday, when the next court hearing in the dispute is scheduled.
Reyes, who was nominated by Joe Biden during his term, wants to know whether federal officials lied about the extent of renovation plans during prior months of hearings.
She also demands to know whether they were truthful about various steps they took, including cutting down hundreds of trees early last month.

Reyes announced during a hearing on 30 October that she was starting a formal investigation into the government’s conduct. Earlier in the case, she had rejected numerous motions from the plaintiffs to step in, saying she trusted the government attorneys.

As the city’s then chief federal prosecutor, Liu oversaw some of the matters referred to her office by then-special counsel Robert Mueller during his investigation into alleged ties between Trump’s 2016 election campaign and Russia .

Trump later nominated her to be associate attorney general, the third-highest-ranking justice department job. Liu withdrew from consideration after running into opposition on the Republican-led Senate judiciary committee because of her past membership in a lawyers’ group that had supported abortion rights.

David Super, a law professor at the Georgetown University law center, said the initiation of a formal investigation by a judge to look into the conduct of a trial’s participants “can be a precursor to holding someone in contempt of court”.

Super said it also is a reflection “of the difficulty she had in determining who initiated the tree-cutting in defiance of the assurances DoJ provided. She doesn’t have the time to keep holding long, complex hearings and so wants a special master to narrow the issues.”

Meanwhile, on Saturday afternoon, Trump posted a long and outlandish message on his social media platform declaring that he was “ordering” the justice department immediately to “look into” Democrats whom he said were “threatening” people in his administration with impeachment, referring to such suggested conduct as a “criminal act”.

The garbled post also accused Democrats of threatening Republican donors and called out the Michigan US senator Elissa Slotkin, a Democrat, saying she was “going after” young people who “give even the slightest inclination to be a Republican” and that this amounted to extortion. The US president did not present further detail or explanation of his claims.
body_zh: 法官将任命特别法官来确定特朗普律师是否在高尔夫球场问题上故意误导她华盛顿特区
安娜·雷耶斯想知道联邦官员是否对东波托马克高尔夫球场的改造计划撒了谎
一名联邦法官周六表示，她打算任命一名在唐纳德·特朗普第一任期内任职的前联邦高级检察官，调查她是否因华盛顿特区一座历史悠久的公共高尔夫球场的改变而被律师和政府官员故意误导。
哥伦比亚特区前美国检察官杰西·刘(Jessie Liu)将调查内政部和国家公园管理局的官员以及司法部的律师在华盛顿保护联盟和两名高尔夫球手于二月份提起的民事案件过程中是否违反道德或误导美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯(Ana Reyes)。
这起诉讼对美国总统在首都周边的一系列建设项目之一提出了挑战——在本案中，是对波托马克河沿岸一个公共高尔夫设施的改造，该项目不像他的其他一些计划那么引人注目，但仍然激怒了许多人。
共和党政府计划于11月15日关闭东波托马克高尔夫球场和公园，目的是建设一个所谓的“能够举办重大赛事的世界级、锦标赛级高尔夫球场”。
雷耶斯上个月发布的一项禁令暂时禁止政府移除或损坏球场上的任何其他树木，并命令管理部门在诉讼进行期间，在对球场的任何“形式或功能”进行任何“不可挽回的修改”之前，提前 10 天发出书面通知。
雷耶斯现在让双方都有机会听取她任命刘作为此案特别主审的计划。他们必须在周五之前以书面形式提出，届时该纠纷的下一次法庭听证会将会安排。
雷耶斯在任期内由乔·拜登提名，他想知道联邦官员在前几个月的听证会上是否对翻修计划的范围撒了谎。
她还要求知道他们所采取的各种措施是否属实，包括上月初砍伐了数百棵树。
雷耶斯在 10 月 30 日的听证会上宣布，她将开始对政府的行为进行正式调查。在此案早些时候，她拒绝了原告提出的多项介入动议，称她信任政府律师。
作为该市时任首席联邦检察官，刘负责监督时任特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒(Robert Mueller)在调查特朗普2016年竞选活动与俄罗斯之间涉嫌关系期间向其办公室转交的一些事务。
特朗普后来提名她担任副司法部长，这是司法部排名第三的职位。刘因过去是支持堕胎权的律师团体的成员，在共和党领导的参议院司法委员会遭到反对后退出了考虑。
乔治城大学法律中心的法学教授大卫·苏珀表示，法官启动正式调查以调查审判参与者的行为“可能是判定某人藐视法庭的先兆”。
超级说，这也反映出“她在确定谁发起了砍伐树木的行为时遇到了困难，无视司法部提供的保证。她没有时间继续举行漫长而复杂的听证会，因此希望有一位特别的大师来缩小问题范围。”
与此同时，周六下午，特朗普在他的社交媒体平台上发布了一条长而古怪的信息，宣称他正在“命令”司法部立即“调查”民主党人，他称这些民主党人用弹劾“威胁”他的政府人员，并将此类建议的行为称为“犯罪行为”。
这篇乱码帖子还指责民主党威胁共和党捐助者，并指责美国密歇根州民主党参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金(Elissa Slotkin)，称她正在“追捕”那些“哪怕有一丝一毫成为共和党倾向”的年轻人，这相当于敲诈勒索。美国总统没有提供进一步的细节或解释他的说法。

title_en: Why this GOP governor thinks his party got ‘worse than a butt whipping’ on Tuesday
title_zh: 为什么这位共和党州长认为他的政党周二“比鞭打屁股更糟糕”
summary: Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt blamed the lack of ‘civility’ from President Trump as a reason Republicans got shellacked.
summary_zh: 俄克拉荷马州州长凯文·斯蒂特指责特朗普总统缺乏“礼貌”是共和党遭到猛烈抨击的原因。
body_en: Kevin Stitt, the outgoing Republican governor of Oklahoma, has a message for President Donald Trump: Try being nice.

“People are just kind of tired,” Stitt told POLITICO in an interview Friday morning, three days after the Republican Party suffered devastating election losses across the country and a few hours before Trump elevated Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff.

“They are just ready for something new and a change ... President Trump’s policies are amazing, and he does a really good job on a lot of fronts, but the civility and then just trying to be nice to people, I think would go a long way.”

Stitt, who was until this summer chair of the National Governors Association, has been in Trump’s crosshairs before. In February, Trump lashed out at Stitt in a dispute over the annual NGA gathering at the White House, calling the Oklahoma governor a “ RINO ” and a “ wiseguy .” The two later appeared to patch things up , after a White House sit-down in March.
Stitt is now one of several prominent Republicans calling on the president and congressional leaders to take stock of the party’s midterm losses and change course heading into 2028.
Asked on Friday if Trump had been nice to him, Stitt laughed, before replying: “I’ve always gotten along with President Trump. He’s always been good to me.”

But the term-limited governor, who has said he intends to return to the private sector next year, did not shy away from calling out the president. Stitt urged Trump to stop directing the Department of Justice to go after his political opponents — tactics the governor described as “Third World country stuff” — and use his final two years in the White House to seriously pursue bipartisan immigration reform.
This transcript has been edited for length and clarity.
You called last year’s election results a “ butt whipping ” for the party. If 2025 was a butt whipping, what was 2026?

Oh man! I don't swear, but it's probably worse than a butt whipping. It was pretty bad. But here's the deal: I think it didn't go the way that we had hoped, but I just want everybody to know, it's not the end of the world. We're all Americans, and it really shows you that we're not as partisan as we think. In other words, the American people can swing both directions, right? That’s a positive.
Our leadership matters, the way we conduct ourselves matters. The American people wanted something different, and I think in two years we'll see what happens.
I think [Texas Gov. Greg] Abbott's loss was really the most shocking to me because he's such a good guy and has been a great governor for Texas, and I don't think anybody saw that coming.
What happened? Why do you think the results went the way they did?

People are tired of the self-dealing that they see in politicians. They see people going to Congress and getting rich, and government contracts to big business. I think people are just really, really cranky right now. Obviously, the kitchen table issues like diesel prices are super hard on the average American, and things are costing more, and I think people are frustrated.

We've got to get back to talking about spending. The national debt [is] out of control. We're spending $2 trillion. It doesn't matter if Republicans or Democrats are in office. People don't even talk about tax policy anymore because they think they can spend whatever they want, regardless of income, and that is driving things up.

We have got to have permitting reform done. If you think about why are gas prices so expensive, part of that you could blame on the war in Iran, but a lot of it is the lack of development of new gas processing pipelines. It takes us eight years to build things anymore, and we have so squashed the private sector from meeting the needs of Americans through over-regulation.
Do Republicans need to do a better job of messaging?
They need to do a better job of messaging. But they also need to do a better job of leading when we get there.

I think the American people are so tired of weaponizing the Department of Justice. When President [Joe] Biden, his party was raiding Mar-a-Lago, they were suing President Trump, and then Trump wins big. I wish that we wouldn't have flipped the script and started weaponizing and going after political opponents. This is Third World country stuff. We have got to stop that.

Now, when the Democrats are in power, if they try to start impeaching Trump again and try weaponizing and investigating instead of leading, I think the American people are going to be frustrated in two years again.
body_zh: 即将卸任的俄克拉荷马州共和党州长凯文·斯蒂特向唐纳德·特朗普总统传达了一条信息：尝试表现得友善。
“人们只是有点累了，”斯蒂特周五早上在接受《政治》杂志采访时表示，三天前，共和党在全国范围内遭受了毁灭性的选举失败，而就在特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为幕僚长的几个小时前。
“他们刚刚准备好迎接新的事物和改变……特朗普总统的政策令人惊叹，他在很多方面都做得非常好，但我认为，礼貌以及努力善待人们会大有帮助。”
斯蒂特今年夏天之前一直担任全国州长协会主席，此前一直是特朗普的攻击目标。今年 2 月，特朗普在白宫年度 NGA 聚会的争议中猛烈抨击了斯蒂特，称这位俄克拉荷马州州长为“绿诺”和“智者”。三月份在白宫举行会谈后，两人似乎和解了。
斯蒂特现在是呼吁总统和国会领导人评估该党中期损失并在 2028 年改变路线的几位知名共和党人之一。
周五，当被问及特朗普是否对他很好时，斯蒂特笑了，然后回答道：“我一直和特朗普总统相处得很好。他一直对我很好。”
但这位任期有限的州长表示，他打算明年重返私营部门，他并没有回避对总统的指责。斯蒂特敦促特朗普停止指示司法部追捕他的政治对手——州长称这种策略为“第三世界国家的东西”——并利用他在白宫的最后两年认真推行两党移民改革。
为了篇幅和清晰度，本文字记录已被编辑。
您称去年的选举结果是对该党的“鞭打”。如果 2025 年是一场鞭打，那么 2026 年又是什么？
天啊！我不发誓，但这可能比鞭打屁股更糟糕。情况非常糟糕。但事情是这样的：我认为事情没有像我们希望的那样发展，但我只是想让每个人都知道，这不是世界末日。我们都是美国人，这确实表明我们并不像我们想象的那样有党派之争。换句话说，美国人民可以双向摇摆，对吗？这是积极的。
我们的领导力很重要，我们的行为方式也很重要。美国人民想要一些不同的东西，我想两年后我们就会看到会发生什么。
我认为[德克萨斯州州长格雷格]阿博特的失败对我来说确实是最令人震惊的，因为他是一个非常好的人，并且一直是德克萨斯州一位伟大的州长，我认为没有人预见到这一点。
发生了什么？您认为为什么会出现这样的结果？
人们厌倦了政客的自我交易。他们看到人们进入国会并致富，政府与大企业签订合同。我认为人们现在真的非常非常暴躁。显然，像柴油价格这样的厨房餐桌问题对普通美国人来说非常困难，而且东西的成本越来越高，我认为人们感到沮丧。
我们必须回到谈论支出。国家债务已经失控。我们花费了 2 万亿美元。共和党或民主党执政并不重要。人们甚至不再谈论税收政策，因为他们认为无论收入如何，他们都可以随心所欲地消费，而这正在推动事情的发展。
我们必须进行许可改革。如果你想一想为什么天然气价格如此昂贵，部分原因可以归咎于伊朗战争，但很大程度上是因为缺乏新的天然气加工管道的开发。我们不再需要八年的时间来建造东西，而且我们通过过度监管压制了私营部门满足美国人的需求。
共和党人需要更好地传达信息吗？
他们需要更好地传达信息。但当我们到达那里时，他们还需要更好地领导。
我认为美国人民已经厌倦了将司法部武器化。当拜登总统和他的政党袭击海湖庄园时，他们起诉特朗普总统，然后特朗普大获全胜。我希望我们不会翻转剧本并开始武器化并追捕政治对手。这是第三世界国家的东西。我们必须阻止这种情况。
现在，当民主党掌权时，如果他们试图再次开始弹劾特朗普，并尝试武器化和调查而不是领导，我认为美国人民将在两年内再次感到沮丧。

title_en: Stephen Miller, Trump’s incoming chief of staff, pledges ‘total devotion’ to the president
title_zh: 特朗普即将上任的幕僚长斯蒂芬·米勒承诺“全身心投入”总统
summary: Hardline aide offers ‘unwavering commitment’ to president amid fears White House will double down on far-right immigration agenda Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, has lavished prai
summary_zh: 由于担心白宫将在极右翼移民议程上加倍努力，强硬派助手向总统提出“坚定不移的承诺”斯蒂芬·米勒，多纳
body_en: Stephen Miller, Trump’s incoming chief of staff, pledges ‘total devotion’ to the president | Trump administration
Hardline aide offers ‘unwavering commitment’ to president amid fears White House will double down on far-right immigration agenda

Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, has lavished praise on the president after his appointment as White House chief of staff.

In his first public remarks since the move was announced, Miller – who begins the role on Monday – pledged “total devotion” to Trump amid concern the administration is now poised to double down on its far-right, nativist immigration agenda.

“If it wasn’t for President Trump the United States of America would not exist right now,” Miller, standing alongside his boss, declared at an event on Friday evening. “This man saved America. He saved our military from collapse. He saved our economy from destruction. He saved our border from annihilation. He saved our country from threats at home and abroad which would have been the end of the American dream for ever.”
Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller a middle finger to millions of voters

His appointment was unveiled after Americans punished Trump’s Republican party in this week’s US midterm elections, unleashing a blue wave that swept through parts of the country where Democrats have not won in decades.

As of Saturday morning, Republicans have lost seven seats in the Senate, and Democrats hold narrow leads in the two races – Alaska and Mississippi – that have yet to be called. Republicans have also lost 42 seats in the House of Representatives, and five governor races.

Despite this extraordinary array of losses nationwide – which senior Republicans including JD Vance have blamed on the Iran war and tariffs , key pillars of Trump’s agenda – Miller praised the president on Friday for having “saved the Republican party from the ash heap of history and has made it stronger, more popular and more resilient than ever before”.

Miller added: “It is the honor of my life to be President Trump’s chief of staff, and I swear to you, and I pledge to you, Mr President, my absolute loyalty, my unwavering commitment, and my total devotion to your success and the success of this country.”

The speech will likely add to concerns that the Trump administration is set to continue pursuing its hardline immigration agenda, which Miller had been leading in his previous role as deputy chief of staff.

Republicans including longtime Trump ally and adviser Roger Stone and party operative Caroline Wren described Miller as the president’s “wartime consigliere”, drawing a sharp line under Trump’s vague suggestions in recent days that he could seek to work with Democrats after they won back control of the US Congress.

Miller’s appointment has been met with dismay by Democrats and some Republicans, with Marlin Stutzman, the Republican congressman from Indiana, describing the move as a “horrible decision” in comments to Politico .

Don Bacon, the outgoing Republican congressman from Nebraska, predicted that Miller will “have an antagonistic relationship with many”, telling CNN : “He cost us seats in Texas and Arizona by alienating many Hispanic voters who voted for Trump in 2024.”
Miller’s appointment was announced as Trump said he expects to make “a few changes” to his team.
“I love my cabinet. I think they’re good. But I’ll do – be doing maybe a few changes. I don’t want to mention who,” Trump told 60 Minutes , in an interview due to air on Sunday.

Asked if he has confidence in his defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, who has faced questions over his future in the role as the scale of the Republicans’ midterm losses became clear, Trump said “I do”, but notably stopped short of crediting him for what the president said were military successes.
Last month, after reports he might replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, Trump was unequivocal: there is “zero chance” that will happen, he told reporters.
body_zh: 特朗普即将上任的幕僚长斯蒂芬·米勒承诺“全身心投入”总统|特朗普政府
由于担心白宫将在极右翼移民议程上加倍努力，强硬派助手向总统提出“坚定不移的承诺”
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)最具争议的助手、全面打击移民行动的策划者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)将在共和党在美国中期选举中失去对美国国会的控制权几天后成为他的新任白宫办公厅主任。
米勒周一上任，在此举宣布以来的首次公开讲话中，他承诺“全力支持”特朗普，因为人们担心政府现在准备加倍推行其极右翼、本土主义移民议程。
“如果没有特朗普总统，美利坚合众国现在就不会存在，”米勒站在他的老板旁边，在周五晚上的一次活动中宣称。 “这个人拯救了美国。他拯救了我们的军队免于崩溃。他拯救了我们的经济免遭破坏。他拯救了我们的边境免遭毁灭。他拯救了我们的国家免受国内外的威胁，这将永远是美国梦的终结。”
特朗普向数百万选民竖起中指
他的任命是在美国人在本周的美国中期选举中惩罚了特朗普领导的共和党之后公布的，掀起了一股蓝色浪潮，席卷了民主党几十年来从未获胜的部分地区。
截至周六上午，共和党在参议院失去了七个席位，民主党在阿拉斯加州和密西西比州这两个尚未公布的竞选中以微弱优势领先。共和党还失去了 42 个众议院席位和 5 个州长竞选席位。
尽管全国范围内遭受了一系列非同寻常的损失——包括万斯在内的共和党资深人士将其归咎于伊朗战争和关税，这是特朗普议程的关键支柱——但米勒周五称赞总统“将共和党从历史的垃圾堆中拯救出来，并使其比以往任何时候都更强大、更受欢迎、更有韧性”。
米勒补充道：“成为特朗普总统的幕僚长是我一生的荣幸，我向你发誓，并向你保证，总统先生，我绝对忠诚，我坚定不移的承诺，我将完全奉献给你的成功和这个国家的成功。”
这次演讲可能会加剧人们对特朗普政府将继续推行强硬移民议程的担忧，米勒在担任副幕僚长之前一直领导着这一议程。
特朗普的长期盟友兼顾问罗杰·斯通(Roger Stone)和党内工作人员卡罗琳·雷恩(Caroline Wren)等共和党人将米勒描述为总统的“战时参谋”，这与特朗普最近几天含糊的暗示，即在民主党重新赢得美国国会控制权后，他可能寻求与民主党合作，这与特朗普的“战时参谋”划清了界限。
米勒的任命令民主党人和一些共和党人感到沮丧，来自印第安纳州的共和党国会议员马林·斯塔茨曼在接受《政治》杂志采访时称此举是一个“可怕的决定”。
即将离任的内布拉斯加州共和党议员唐·培根 (Don Bacon) 预测米勒将“与许多人产生敌对关系”，他告诉 CNN：“他疏远了许多在 2024 年投票给特朗普的拉美裔选民，从而让我们失去了德克萨斯州和亚利桑那州的席位。”
米勒的任命是在特朗普表示他希望对他的团队做出“一些改变”时宣布的。
“我爱我的内阁。我认为他们很好。但我会做的——也许会做一些改变。我不想提及是谁，”特朗普在周日播出的《60 分钟》采访中说道。
当被问及他对国防部长皮特·赫格斯是否有信心时，特朗普说“我有信心”，但没有将总统所说的军事成功归功于他。随着共和党中期选举的失败规模变得明朗，他的国防部长皮特·赫格斯的未来面临着质疑。
上个月，在有报道称他可能取代苏西·威尔斯担任白宫办公厅主任后，特朗普对记者明确表示：这种情况发生的“可能性为零”。

title_en: The Trump administration wants underwater datacenters. One Great Lakes non-profit is already preparing
title_zh: 特朗普政府想要水下数据中心。 One Great Lakes 非营利组织已经在准备
summary: Tech companies like the idea, as they largely eliminate community opposition, and could cut down on utility costs While Elon Musk has often touted putting datacenters in space, reports suggest that another geographic area may soon become a widespread target: o
summary_zh: 科技公司喜欢这个想法，因为它们在很大程度上消除了社区的反对，并且可以降低公用事业成本，而埃隆·马斯克经常吹捧
body_en: The Trump administration wants underwater datacenters. One Great Lakes non-profit is already preparing | Datacenters – US
Tech companies like the idea, as they largely eliminate community opposition, and could cut down on utility costs
While Elon Musk has often touted putting datacenters in space, reports suggest that another geographic area may soon become a widespread target: our lakes and oceans .

Two underwater datacenters are already in operation off the coast of China, and recent reports suggest that the Trump administration is considering plans for four proposed underwater, sealed-pod datacenters to be built off the shores of Maine and Alaska .
At a campaign rally in Ohio last month, Donald Trump said of datacenters: “There’s so much money to be made for Ohio … they’ll go to China … we want them.”

Underwater iterations are particularly attractive to tech companies as they largely eliminate community opposition and controversy around datacenters in residential areas on land. In theory, underwater datacenters could also significantly cut down on utility costs, another issue that’s currently riling communities across the country.

A Microsoft project set up off the coast of northern Scotland in 2018 found that after two years, server failures were reduced by 87% compared with on-land datacenter equivalents. Microsoft executives saw the project, which ended after two years, as an unmitigated success.
That makes the cool, salt-free waters of the Great Lakes, home to 30 million people in major cities such as Chicago, Toronto and Detroit, potentially attractive to datacenter companies.

A spokesperson for the federal Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) said: “The EPA supports development of data center infrastructure that is essential to remaining the world leader in Super Intelligence while using its statutory authorities to protect water quality.”

But the environmental consequences of any similar project in the freshwater Great Lakes, which those tens of millions of people depend on for drinking water every day, could be significant. Local environmental activists are already worried and sounding the alarm – even though no underwater datacenter projects are currently proposed for the region.
For them, they think it is better to be prepared than surprised, given the high stakes of the ecologically sensitive ecosystem.

“We are concerned because if you think about what a datacenter does, it throws off a lot of heat. Lake Erie already has an issue with harmful algal blooms, and they develop because of heat, not only because of fertilizers and agricultural runoff,” said John Lipaj of the Lake Erie Foundation , a non-profit based in Ohio.

The floor of Lake Erie on the US side falls under the jurisdiction of the state of Ohio. In the past, its state government, where Republicans hold a supermajority, proposed a law making it easier for datacenter companies to discharge wastewater into public waterways. That measure was denied by the state’s EPA last July following a public outcry. Of the eight US Great Lakes states, only New York currently has a temporary state-wide moratorium on datacenter construction. That ends in mid-2027.
“We’re also concerned about the possibility of contamination and leaks. These have not been around a long time,” said Lipaj.

“We are concerned about the types of fluid contained in a datacenter, the batteries and electrical equipment. These are all things that could lead to a catastrophic failure that we don’t want happening in the Great Lakes.”

Lake Erie is home or close to major cities such as Cleveland, Detroit and Buffalo and is already by far the warmest of the five Great Lakes during summer months. It also ranks as one of the most polluted large lakes in the country in large part due to agricultural runoff in its western basin. A number of fish species are under threat due to the lake’s warming trend.

“Warm water can impact aquatic life and ecosystems in a number of ways. One immediate effect is what is known as a thermal shock,” said Helena Volzer of the Alliance for the Great Lakes, an environmental group based in Chicago.

“Aquatic organisms are highly sensitive to temperature changes, and even a small, rapid increase of just 2-5F can be dramatic for the aquatic ecosystem. When a facility releases warm water, it can alter metabolism and increase oxygen demand, reduce dissolved oxygen availability, disrupt food webs [and] force fish to move away from preferred habitats.”

On 3 November, residents of Conneaut, a Lake Erie community of about 12,000 people an hour’s drive north-east of Cleveland, voted in favor of a charter amendment to prohibit the construction of large datacenters in its area.
body_zh: 特朗普政府想要水下数据中心。 One Great Lakes 非营利组织已经在准备 |数据中心 – 美国
科技公司喜欢这个想法，因为它们在很大程度上消除了社区的反对，并且可以降低公用事业成本
虽然埃隆·马斯克经常吹捧将数据中心放在太空中，但有报告表明，另一个地理区域可能很快就会成为广泛的目标：我们的湖泊和海洋。
两个水下数据中心已经在中国沿海投入运行，最近的报告表明，特朗普政府正在考虑在缅因州和阿拉斯加海岸建造四个拟议的水下密封舱数据中心的计划。
在上个月在俄亥俄州举行的一次竞选集会上，唐纳德·特朗普谈到了数据中心： “俄亥俄州有很多钱可以赚……他们会去中国……我们想要他们。”
水下迭代对科技公司特别有吸引力，因为它们在很大程度上消除了社区对陆地住宅区数据中心的反对和争议。从理论上讲，水下数据中心还可以显着降低公用事业成本，这是目前困扰全国各地社区的另一个问题。
2018 年在苏格兰北部海岸设立的一个微软项目发现，两年后，与陆地数据中心同等情况相比，服务器故障减少了 87%。微软高管认为这个两年后结束的项目取得了彻底的成功。
这使得芝加哥、多伦多和底特律等主要城市拥有 3000 万人口的五大湖凉爽、无盐的水域对数据中心公司具有潜在的吸引力。
美国联邦环境保护局 (EPA) 的一位发言人表示：“EPA 支持数据中心基础设施的开发，这对于保持超级智能的世界领先地位至关重要，同时利用其法定权限来保护水质。”
但在淡水五大湖中任何类似的项目都会造成严重的环境后果，数以千万计的人们每天都依赖这些湖来获取饮用水。尽管目前尚未为该地区提出水下数据中心项目，但当地环保活动人士已经感到担忧并敲响了警钟。
对他们来说，考虑到生态敏感的生态系统的高风险，他们认为做好准备比感到惊讶更好。
“我们很担心，因为如果你考虑一下数据中心的作用，就会发现它会散发出大量热量。伊利湖已经存在有害藻华的问题，它们的发展是因为热量，而不仅仅是因为化肥和农业径流，”俄亥俄州非营利组织伊利湖基金会的约翰·利帕杰(John Lipaj)说。
伊利湖美国一侧的湖底属于俄亥俄州管辖。过去，共和党占绝对多数的州政府提出了一项法律，使数据中心公司更容易将废水排放到公共水道中。去年 7 月，由于公众强烈抗议，该措施被该州环保局否决。在美国五大湖区的八个州中，目前只有纽约在全州范围内临时暂停数据中心建设。到 2027 年中期结束。
“我们还担心污染和泄漏的可能性。这些问题出现的时间并不长，”利帕杰说。
“我们担心数据中心、电池和电气设备中所含流体的类型。这些都可能导致灾难性故障，我们不希望在五大湖发生这种情况。”
伊利湖位于克利夫兰、底特律和布法罗等主要城市的所在地或附近，并且是迄今为止五大湖中夏季最温暖的湖。它还被列为该国污染最严重的大型湖泊之一，这在很大程度上是由于其西部流域的农业径流造成的。由于湖泊变暖的趋势，许多鱼类受到威胁。
“温暖的水可以通过多种方式影响水生生物和生态系统。其中一个直接影响就是所谓的热冲击，”总部位于芝加哥的环保组织五大湖联盟的海伦娜·沃尔泽说。
“水生生物对温度变化高度敏感，即使是 2-5 华氏度的小幅快速升温也会对水生生态系统产生巨大影响。当设施释放温水时，它会改变新陈代谢并增加需氧量，减少溶解氧的可用性，破坏食物网[并]迫使鱼类远离首选栖息地。”
11 月 3 日，康尼奥特 (Conneaut) 的居民投票支持一项宪章修正案，禁止在该地区建设大型数据中心。康尼奥特是伊利湖社区，距离克利夫兰东北部约 12,000 人，车程约 1 小时。

title_en: Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller is a middle finger to millions of voters
title_zh: 特朗普对斯蒂芬·米勒的提升是对数百万选民的中指
summary: Architect of Trump’s far-right immigration agenda is now most powerful unelected figure in government – it suggests White House is moving to a war footing Donald Trump just gave the middle finger to millions of American voters. Any other president who suffered
summary_zh: 特朗普极右移民议程的设计师现在是政府中最有权势的非民选人物——这表明白宫正在走向一场战争
body_en: Architect of Trump’s far-right immigration agenda is now most powerful unelected figure in government – it suggests White House is moving to a war footing
Donald Trump just gave the middle finger to millions of American voters.

Any other president who suffered the kind of drubbing at the polls that Trump did this week might have felt at least a sliver of humility – and perhaps even an obligation to work with the new opposition in Congress.

But not for the first time in his political career, Trump veered in the opposite direction. On Friday he made Stephen Miller, condemned by Democrats and civil rights groups as a white nationalist, one of the most powerful unelected officials in Washington by naming him White House chief of staff .
What happens after the ‘blue wave’? Your questions on the US midterm election results answered

Miller is the architect of Trump’s far-right, nativist immigration agenda. He is, therefore, arguably the architect of the blue wave that engulfed Republicans in Tuesday’s midterm elections as voters – including many Latinos – expressed their disgust. Yet instead of firing Miller, Trump promoted him.

It was a declaration of war. Miller, 41, is a longtime proponent of the presidential authority that Trump has spent the past two years expanding at the expense of Congress. In 2017 he declared : “The powers of the president to protect our country are very substantial and will not be questioned.”
Now Republicans’ catastrophic defeat is likely to leave Trump more reliant on unilateral executive action than ever to advance his domestic agenda.

“In a lot of ways Stephen Miller has been the id to Trump’s authoritarian impulses and machinations,” Kurt Bardella , an adviser to Democrats in Texas, said. “I have to imagine that anointing this person chief of staff – the most powerful non-elected position in all of government – is a signal that they intend to double down on that authoritarianism.
“You’re going to see a lot of executive orders, unilateral action and stress testing of the checks and balances system continue for the final two years of his presidency.”

Trump’s second term has presented a concerted effort to dismantle those checks and balances that have traditionally constrained the occupant of the White House. He has signed 292 executive orders in less than two years, more than in his entire first term and a record pace for a modern presidency.

He has bypassed Congress on military action and tariffs, withheld congressionally approved spending, deployed the National Guard against the will of state authorities, politicised the justice department, punished critics and challenged judicial independence. Congress, dominated by Republicans reluctant to confront him, offered little resistance.

But this week’s landslide , the biggest in a midterm election since Watergate, puts Democrats back in charge of the House of Representatives and Senate. That the elections were free and fair, and that Trump did not dispute the result, was itself a victory for democracy.

Democrats will now seek to rein in the president and block his legislative agenda, bringing them into direct conflict with Miller, who was already a hugely powerful deputy chief of staff at the White House and now takes over from Susie Wiles .

Miller has been a champion of the Iran war and prominent voice on many of the president’s other priorities, including countering diversity initiatives and targeting transgender rights. He is reportedly one of a small group of White House staffers who approve all executive orders.

He is best known for driving the ‌immigration crackdown in Trump’s second term, setting ‌a target of 3,000 arrests per day – far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to target anybody in ‌the country illegally, not just those with criminal records.

There are limits on what Democrats can do to stop the immigration drive since the One Big Beautiful Bill Act included major increases for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that will keep it funded for the rest of Trump’s term.

Even so, they will now chair House committees with the ability to launch investigations, issue subpoenas and hold high profile hearings. Along with ICE, they might scrutinise Jeffrey Epstein files and the department of government efficiency (Doge). They have also vowed to look at how Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office.

The appointment of the pugnacious Miller as Trump’s consigliere suggests that the White House is moving to a war footing. He is likely to marshal a team of lawyers and attack Democrats by accusing them of weaponising the deep state against the president. As a frequent guest on the conservative Fox News network, he will also wage war in the court of public opinion.
body_zh: 特朗普极右移民议程的设计者现在是政府中最有权势的非民选人物——这表明白宫正在进入战争状态
唐纳德·特朗普刚刚向数百万美国选民竖起了中指。
任何其他在民意调查中遭受特朗普本周惨败的总统可能至少会感到一丝谦卑 — — 甚至可能有义务与国会的新反对派合作。
但这并不是特朗普在其政治生涯中第一次转向相反的方向。周五，他任命斯蒂芬·米勒为白宫幕僚长，使他成为华盛顿最有权势的非民选官员之一，民主党和民权组织谴责他是白人民族主义者。
“蓝色浪潮”之后会发生什么？您对美国中期选举结果的疑问得到解答
米勒是特朗普极右翼本土主义移民议程的设计师。因此，他可以说是周二中期选举中席卷共和党的蓝色浪潮的缔造者，因为选民——包括许多拉丁裔——表达了他们的厌恶。然而，特朗普并没有解雇米勒，而是提拔了他。
这是宣战。 41 岁的米勒是特朗普过去两年以牺牲国会为代价扩大总统权力的长期支持者。 2017年，他宣称：“总统保护我们国家的权力非常重大，不会受到质疑。”
现在，共和党的灾难性失败可能会让特朗普比以往任何时候都更加依赖单边行政行动来推进其国内议程。
“在很多方面，斯蒂芬·米勒都是特朗普独裁冲动和阴谋的体现，”得克萨斯州民主党顾问库尔特·巴尔德拉(Kurt Bardella)说。 “我不得不想象，任命这位幕僚长——整个政府中最有权势的非民选职位——是一个信号，表明他们打算加倍推行威权主义。
“在他总统任期的最后两年里，你会看到大量行政命令、单边行动以及对制衡体系的压力测试仍在继续。”
特朗普的第二个任期提出了一项共同努力，以废除传统上限制白宫主人的制衡机制。他在不到两年的时间里签署了 292 项行政命令，比他整个第一个任期的签署数量还要多，创下了现代总统任期的纪录。
他在军事行动和关税问题上绕过国会，扣留国会批准的支出，违背州当局的意愿部署国民警卫队，将司法部门政治化，惩罚批评者并挑战司法独立。由不愿与他对抗的共和党人主导的国会几乎没有做出任何抵抗。
但本周的压倒性胜利是自水门事件以来中期选举中最大的一次，使民主党重新掌控众议院和参议院。选举是自由和公平的，特朗普也没有对结果提出异议，这本身就是民主的胜利。
民主党人现在将寻求控制总统并阻止他的立法议程，从而使他们与米勒发生直接冲突，米勒已经是白宫权力极大的副幕僚长，现在接替了苏西·怀尔斯。
米勒一直是伊朗战争的支持者，并在总统的许多其他优先事项上发表了突出的声音，包括反对多元化倡议和针对变性人权利。据报道，他是批准所有行政命令的一小群白宫工作人员之一。
他因在特朗普第二任期内推动移民镇压而闻名，设定了每天逮捕 3,000 人的目标——远远高于前几届政府的水平。他敦促移民和海关执法局（ICE）针对该国境内的任何非法人士，而不仅仅是那些有犯罪记录的人。
由于《美丽法案法案》包括对移民和海关执法局（ICE）的大幅增加，这将在特朗普剩余任期内为其提供资金支持，因此民主党在阻止移民运动方面所能采取的措施是有限的。
即便如此，他们现在将担任众议院委员会主席，有权发起调查、发出传票并举行高调的听证会。他们可能会与 ICE 一起审查杰弗里·爱泼斯坦 (Jeffrey Epstein) 的档案和政府效率部 (Doge)。他们还发誓要研究特朗普及其家人自特朗普重返办公室以来如何变得更加富有。
好斗的米勒被任命为特朗普的顾问，这表明白宫正在进入战争状态。他可能会组建一支律师团队，攻击民主党人，指责他们将深层政府武器化来对抗总统。作为保守派福克斯新闻网的常客，他也将在舆论法庭上发动战争。

title_en: Wisconsin state patrol trooper detained by ICE released from custody
title_zh: 被 ICE 拘留的威斯康星州巡逻队员已获释
summary: Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe immigrated to US at 14 and has been waiting seven years for asylum case to be heard A Wisconsin state patrol trooper, whom federal immigration agents detained on Thursday at an airport, has been released from their custody. Immigratio
summary_zh: Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe 14 岁时移民到美国，为庇护案件的审理已经等待了七年。
body_en: Wisconsin state patrol trooper detained by ICE released from custody | Wisconsin
Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe immigrated to US at 14 and has been waiting seven years for asylum case to be heard
A Wisconsin state patrol trooper, whom federal immigration agents detained on Thursday at an airport, has been released from their custody.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents approached Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, a South African national, as he waited to board a domestic flight, according to his law firm Christopher & De León.

Van Der Merwe, who immigrated to the US when he was 14, has been waiting seven years for his asylum case to be heard, his attorneys said in social media posts. In the meantime, he received work authorization, valid through 2030, to serve in Wisconsin’s law enforcement.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) defended Van Der Merwe’s detention in a statement this week, saying he had overstayed a 2019 visa. “Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the US,” an agency spokesperson told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.
Van Der Merwe’s lawyers rejected that claim, noting that another DHS agency, US Citizenship and Immigration Services, “authorized him to work”.
“We don’t think ICE even believes its own statement,” the law firm added.
The agency did not immediately respond to an inquiry about what prompted the state trooper’s release.
In a social media update on Friday, Van Der Merwe’s law firm shared that their client would be released, but subject to electronic monitoring and regular check-ins with immigration authorities.
“His release is welcome news. But our fight is not over. Carel will still have to defend his immigration case before an immigration judge,” the attorneys wrote.

“USCIS, an agency within DHS, authorized Carel to work. He used that authorization to serve and protect Wisconsin communities. ICE, another agency within DHS, then detained him. DHS owes this family more than silence,” they continued.
Video of Van Der Merwe’s graduation ceremony last year showed that his badge was pinned on by his father in front of Wisconsin’s governor.

Van Der Merwe’s family of white South Africans arrived during Donald Trump’s first term, but they had good reason to expect that they would be granted asylum after Trump returned to office last year and signed an executive order saying the US would “promote the resettlement of Afrikaner refugees”, based on the false claim that they would be “escaping government-sponsored race-based discrimination” at home.

In addition to a series of highly public, contentious and in some cases deadly ICE raids across several US cities, the Trump administration’s mass deportation agenda has played out more furtively at domestic and international airports. Travelers with visas, green-card holders and pending asylum cases have been detained in what some experts say is an effort to meet arrest quotas imposed on the agency by the White House.
Van Der Merwe’s law firm advised noncitizens with unresolved immigration paperwork to consult immigration attorneys before traveling by air.
“Even if you have flown without problems before, do not assume the same will happen now,” they said.
body_zh: 被 ICE 拘留的威斯康星州巡逻队员已获释威斯康星州
Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe 14 岁时移民到美国，等待庇护案件审理已经七年了
周四，联邦移民特工在机场拘留了一名威斯康星州巡逻队员，现已被释放。
据克里斯托弗·德莱昂律师事务所称，南非公民卡雷尔·亚伦·范德梅韦 (Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe) 在等待登机时，移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 人员接近了他。
范德默韦 (Van Der Merwe) 14 岁时移民到美国，他的律师在社交媒体帖子中表示，他已经等待庇护案审理七年了。与此同时，他获得了在威斯康星州执法部门任职的工作授权，有效期至 2030 年。
美国国土安全部 (DHS) 在本周的一份声明中为 Van Der Merwe 的拘留辩护，称他已逾期居留 2019 年签证。 “工作授权或待处理的申请并不赋予在美国的合法身份，”该机构发言人告诉《密尔沃基哨兵报》。
范德默韦的律师拒绝了这一说法，并指出另一家国土安全部机构美国公民及移民服务局“授权他工作”。
“我们认为 ICE 甚至不相信自己的声明，”该律师事务所补充道。
该机构没有立即回应有关为何释放该州警的询问。
在周五的社交媒体更新中，范德默韦的律师事务所表示，他们的客户将被释放，但会受到电子监控并定期向移民当局报到。
“他的获释是个好消息。但我们的斗争还没有结束。卡雷尔仍然必须在移民法官面前为他的移民案件辩护，”律师写道。
“国土安全部内的一个机构美国移民局授权卡雷尔工作。他利用该授权来服务和保护威斯康星州社区。国土安全部内的另一个机构移民和海关执法局随后拘留了他。国土安全部欠这个家庭的不仅仅是沉默，”他们继续说道。
去年范德默韦毕业典礼的视频显示，他的徽章是由他的父亲在威斯康星州州长面前别上的。
范德默韦的南非白人家庭是在唐纳德·特朗普的第一个任期内抵达的，但他们有充分的理由预计，在特朗普去年重返办公室后，他们将获得庇护，并签署了一项行政命令，称美国将“促进阿非利卡难民的重新安置”，理由是他们将在国内“逃离政府支持的基于种族的歧视”。
除了在美国多个城市进行一系列高度公开、有争议甚至致命的 ICE 突袭外，特朗普政府的大规模驱逐议程还在国内和国际机场更加秘密地进行。持有签证的旅行者、绿卡持有者和待决的庇护案件被拘留，一些专家称这是为了满足白宫对该机构施加的逮捕配额。
范德默韦的律师事务所建议持有未解决的移民文书的非公民在乘飞机旅行之前咨询移民律师。
他们说：“即使你以前飞行时没有出现任何问题，也不要认为现在会发生同样的情况。”

body_en: Trump says he offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House press secretary role - CBS News
President Trump says he has offered the open White House press secretary role to UFC CEO Dana White.

The president said Saturday in a Truth Social post, "I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States."

"I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris. We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," he said.

It was unclear at the time of publication whether White has accepted the position, though he shared an image of himself at the White House press briefing room podium to his Instagram story with the caption, "On to the next chapter."
Reporting from at least one media outlet suggested that the post may have been made tongue-in-cheek. CBS News has reached out to the White House and UFC for additional comment.
The president's remarks come days after Democrats swept the midterm elections , taking control of the House and the Senate.

The press secretary role has been vacant since Oct. 16, when conservative commentator Katie Zacharia was removed from the job after just five days. Zacharia was Mr. Trump's pick to fill the role after Karoline Leavitt stepped aside in August, saying she wanted to spend more time with her young family.

As the chief of Ultimate Fighting Championship, running a global league valued at more than $15 billion, White has been a longtime supporter of Mr. Trump and attended his inauguration. The White House also hosted an Ultimate Fighting Championship in July on the South Lawn to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. The event coincided with Mr. Trump's 80th birthday.
"Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!" Mr. Trump said in his post.
This is a developing story and will be updated.

title_en: Trump offers press secretary position to UFC head Dana White

summary: President Donald Trump said that he’d offered the job of White House press secretary to the CEO and president of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, Dana White.

body_en: President Donald Trump on Saturday said on Truth Social that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the CEO and president of the Ultimate Fighting Championship.
“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” the president wrote.
Trump suggested in his post that White should bring several UFC fighters, including Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje and Amanda Nunes, as assistants to defend against the “Lunatic Left.”
“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” he added.
Trump and White have long been friends and the president has attended many UFC fights while serving in the White House.
Earlier this year, White also organized a UFC fight on the South Lawn of the White House, an event that was part of a slate commemorating the United States’ 250th birthday.
Many Trump administration officials and Republican lawmakers attended the fight in July.
It’s unclear whether Trump’s offer to White to serve as press secretary is a serious one.
A spokesperson for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The position has been vacant since Katie Zacharia departed the role after just five days in October.

Zacharia had replaced Karoline Leavitt, who served as White House press secretary since Trump returned to office in January of last year. Leavitt announced in August that she would leave her post to spend more time with her family.
The White House had another staff shake-up on Friday, when chief of staff Susie Wiles said she would be stepping down from her post. Trump named longtime aide Stephen Miller as her replacement.
Alexandra Marquez is a politics reporter for NBC News.

title_en: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
title_zh: 美国联邦航空局宣布在佛罗里达州和阿拉斯加建立美国首个数字空中交通管制塔
summary: Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technology The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing n
summary_zh: 系统提供机场运营的 360 度视图，但人们对该技术提出了担忧 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA)
body_en: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska | Trump administration
Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technology

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing new technology first to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska as the Trump administration presses ahead with updating the country’s ageing aviation infrastructure.

The systems are now online at the Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and the Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska, with five additional regional airports slated to receive the technology next.

The digital towers use advanced camera systems and digital displays to give air traffic controllers a continuous, 360-degree view of airport operations, including runways, taxiways and surrounding airspace, according to the agency.
Senate-approved bills aim to ease burden on pilots amid mental health ‘stigma’

The FAA maintains that the technology is not intended to replace human controllers. Instead, the systems are designed to provide greater visibility and additional information to help controllers perform their existing duties.

“Our air traffic controllers continue to do the critical job of keeping aircraft safely separated, and we’re giving them better technology to do that,” said the FAA’s administrator, Bryan Bedford, in a statement .
“Digital towers provide controllers with greater visibility of airport activity and more information to make critical decisions,” he added.

Bedford is scheduled to appear before the House transportation and infrastructure committee next week, where he will face questions about the progress and challenges surrounding the administration’s ongoing $12.5bn modernization initiative.
The effort aims to replace decades-old equipment still used throughout the aviation system, including copper telecommunications lines, floppy disks and paper strips used to track aircraft.

Congress approved $12.5bn over five years in June 2025 to support air traffic control reforms, but the Trump administration is seeking another $30bn from the legislative branch to fund additional improvements.

Concerns about the types of technology being implemented within air traffic control have been gaining traction alongside the increasing unease about artificial intelligence as a whole. In September, the FAA rolled out a new AI software tool called the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (Smart).
Trump has been heavily criticized for his response to a national shortage of air traffic controllers following last year’s government shutdown.

Staffing levels in control towers and many related aspects of US air traffic safety systems have been under especially close scrutiny since a midair collision between a passenger jet and a military helicopter on the outskirts of Washington DC in 2025 that killed 67 people. It was the deadliest crash in the US for more than 20 years and the authorities later deemed it “100% preventable”.
body_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 宣布在佛罗里达州和阿拉斯加建立美国首个数字空中交通管制塔特朗普政府
系统提供机场运营的 360 度视图，但人们对该技术提出了担忧
美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 宣布，美国首座数字空中交通管制塔正式投入运营，随着特朗普政府继续更新美国老化的航空基础设施，该塔将首先为佛罗里达州和阿拉斯加的小型机场带来新技术。
该系统现已在佛罗里达州巴托行政机场 (KBOW) 和阿拉斯加基奈市政机场 (PAEN) 上线，接下来还有另外五个支线机场计划接收该技术。
据该机构称，数字塔使用先进的摄像系统和数字显示器，为空中交通管制员提供机场运营的连续 360 度视图，包括跑道、滑行道和周围空域。
参议院批准的法案旨在减轻飞行员因心理健康“耻辱”而承受的负担
美国联邦航空局坚称，该技术无意取代人类控制人员。相反，这些系统旨在提供更大的可见性和附加信息，以帮助管制员履行现有职责。
美国联邦航空局局长布莱恩·贝德福德 (Bryan Bedford) 在一份声明中表示：“我们的空中交通管制员继续承担保持飞机安全分离的关键工作，我们正在为他们提供更好的技术来做到这一点。”
他补充道：“数字塔台为管制员提供了机场活动的更清晰可见性以及做出关键决策所需的更多信息。”
贝德福德计划​​下周出席众议院交通和基础设施委员会的听证会，届时他将面临有关政府正在进行的 125 亿美元现代化计划的进展和挑战的问题。
这项工作的目的是更换整个航空系统仍在使用的几十年前的设备，包括用于跟踪飞机的铜质电信线路、软盘和纸带。
国会于 2025 年 6 月批准了五年内 125 亿美元的资金来支持空中交通管制改革，但特朗普政府正在寻求立法部门另外提供 300 亿美元来资助进一步的改进。
随着对整个人工智能的不安日益增加，人们对空中交通管制中实施的技术类型的担忧也越来越受到关注。 9月，美国联邦航空局推出了一款新的人工智能软件工具，名为“空域、航线和轨迹战略管理（智能）”。
特朗普因去年政府关门后对全国空中交通管制员短缺的反应而受到严厉批评。
自 2025 年华盛顿特区郊区一架客机与一架军用直升机发生空中相撞事件、造成 67 人死亡以来，控制塔的人员配备水平以及美国空中交通安全系统的许多相关方面一直受到特别密切的审查。这是美国 20 多年来最严重的车祸，当局后来认为这是“100% 可预防的”。

title_en: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
title_zh: 被驱逐的巴拉圭总统出现在检察官面前
summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.
summary_zh: 巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳周五被免职并被软禁。参议院在崩溃后就弹劾他进行了投票
body_en: Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña placed under house arrest : NPR

Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña placed under house arrest Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

Paraguay's President Santiago Peña waves after a meeting with Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez at the Miraflores Presidential Palace in Caracas, on September 19, 2026. Federico Parra/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after the collapse of a prominent U.S.-owned bank with ties to Paraguay's government. The fallout has left millions across the country without access to their money.
Peña is one of Washington's closest allies in the region and was a shareholder in Ueno Bank, a digital lender that served about 3 million customers — more than half of the country's adult population.

He was known as a pro-market leader focused on making it easier to do business in the country, but legislators said he jeopardized state assets and benefitted himself through his connection to the bank.
Ueno Bank previously said more than a million people opened bank accounts for the first time using its services, which included generous cash back offers on groceries.
Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
A trial has proceeded against Peña, and he appeared before prosecutors Saturday morning . The last president ousted from office was Fernando Lugo in 2012.
Peña has denied any wrongdoing but on Thursday he announced his resignation . Lawmakers refused to accept that resignation, and instead moved forward with the country's impeachment process.
At proceedings inside the country's Senate Friday, legislators unanimously found Peña guilty of malfeasance in office, according to the Senate's website .
Prosecutors then accused him of a breach of trust, among other charges, before placing him under house arrest .
"I want to apologize to the Paraguayan people if I have failed you," Peña said in a speech posted to social media.

Demonstrators burn an image depicting Paraguay's President Santiago Pena, during a protest over the banking crisis and his resignation, at the main square in the surroundings of the National Congress in Asuncion, on November 5, 2026. Daniel Duarte/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Pedro Alliana, the country's vice president, was sworn in as president to serve out the rest of Peña's term until August 2028. In a speech on Friday , he announced he would take action to compensate people whose money was lost in the bank's collapse.
Paraguay's central bank said it seized control of Ueno Bank on Tuesday because its solvency ratio, an assessment of a company's long-term financial viability, no longer met legal standards.

Protests erupted across Asunción , the country's capital city, following the seizure.
NPR's John Otis and Catherine Osborn contributed reporting to this story.
body_zh: 巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳被软禁：NPR
巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳被软禁 巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳周五被免职并被软禁。一家国有银行倒闭后，参议院就弹劾他进行了投票。
2026 年 9 月 19 日，巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳在加拉加斯米拉弗洛雷斯总统府与委内瑞拉临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯会面后挥手致意。Federico Parra/法新社（盖蒂图片社）隐藏标题栏
巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳周五因与巴拉圭政府有联系的一家著名美国银行倒闭而被弹劾并被软禁。其后果导致全国数百万人无法获得资金。
佩纳是华盛顿在该地区最亲密的盟友之一，也是上野银行的股东，该银行是一家数字贷款机构，为约 300 万客户（占该国成年人口的一半以上）提供服务。
他被认为是一位亲市场的领导人，致力于让在该国开展业务变得更加容易，但立法者表示，他危害了国有资产，并通过与银行的联系为自己谋取利益。
上野银行此前表示，超过一百万人首次使用其服务开设了银行账户，其中包括对食品杂货的慷慨现金返还优惠。
巴西左翼总统卢拉当选第四任总统
对佩纳的审判已经开始，他于周六上午出庭受审。上一位被赶下台的总统是 2012 年的费尔南多·卢戈。
佩纳否认有任何不当行为，但周四他宣布辞职。议员们拒绝接受这一辞职，而是继续推进该国的弹劾程序。
据参议院网站报道，周五在该国参议院的诉讼程序中，立法者一致判定佩纳犯有职务渎职罪。
检察官随后指控他违反信任等罪名，然后将他软禁。
佩纳在社交媒体上发布的讲话中说：“如果我让你们失望了，我想向巴拉圭人民道歉。”
2026 年 11 月 5 日，示威者在亚松森国民议会周围的主广场上焚烧了一幅描绘巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳的图像，抗议银行业危机和他的辞职。丹尼尔·杜阿尔特/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
